detailed_results.question: Why do veins appear blue?
detailed_results.answer: Veins appear blue due to the way light is absorbed and scattered by the skin and underlying tissues. When light hits the skin, it is mostly reflected back to the surface, but some of it penetrates deeper into the tissue. As the light travels through the tissue, it is absorbed and scattered, with shorter wavelengths (blue) being absorbed more than longer wavelengths (red). This causes the blue light to scatter back up to the surface, making the veins appear blue.
